spec.description: Two circles intersect at A and B. Q, A and P are collinear, in that order; T, B and S are collinear, in that order. Q and T lie on the larger left circle; P and S lie on the smaller right circle. Draw QT, QP, TS, AB and PS. ∠TQA = 70°. α = ∠TBA, β = ∠ABS and γ = ∠APS.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Opposite angles in cyclic QABT give $\alpha=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$. Since T,B,S are collinear, $\beta=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ$. Opposite angles in cyclic APSB give $\gamma=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$.
Since Q,A,P are collinear, $\angle TQP=70^\circ$ and $\angle SPQ=\gamma=110^\circ$. These are supplementary co-interior angles on transversal QP, so $PS\parallel QT$.

spec.description: Two circles intersect at B and A. Q and P lie on the larger left circle; M lies on the smaller right circle. Q, B and M are collinear; P, A and M are collinear. Draw QP, QM, PM and AB. BM and AM carry matching double ticks. ∠PQM = 50°. α = ∠PAB, β = ∠ABM and γ = ∠QPM.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Opposite angles in cyclic QPAB give $\alpha=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ$. Since P,A,M are collinear, $\angle BAM=50^\circ$. As AM=BM, triangle ABM has equal base angles, so $\beta=50^\circ$. Since Q,B,M are collinear, $\angle QBA=130^\circ$. Its opposite cyclic angle is $\gamma=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$.
In part iii, $\angle QPM=\gamma=50^\circ$ and $\angle BAP=\alpha=130^\circ$. They are supplementary co-interior angles on line PM, so $AB\parallel PQ$.

Triangle PQM has equal angles $\angle QPM=\angle PQM=50^\circ$, so $MP=MQ$. Also MA=MB is given. Since P,A,M and Q,B,M occur in those orders, subtracting the equal inner lengths gives $AP=MP-MA=MQ-MB=BQ$.
